comparisons.peer_topic: Remaining Performance Obligations Balance and Recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose future/remaining performance obligations exceeding one year, indicating backlog or long-term contractual commitments. MU reports $141 million in future performance obligations beyond one year, which explicitly includes $907 million in customer prepayments and other contract liabilities. AMD reports a significantly smaller amount of $85 million in aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months. Both disclosures relate to revenue allocation for unsatisfied performance obligations, though the magnitude and composition (specifically the inclusion of large prepayments in MU's figure) differ substantially.

sentences.text: As of August 29, 2024, our future performance obligations beyond one year were $141 million, which included customer prepayments and other contract liabilities.

Customer prepayments made to secure product supply in future periods and other contract liabilities were $907 million as of August 29, 2024, of which $766 million was reported in other current liabilities and the remainder in other noncurrent liabilities.

As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.

comparisons.peer_topic: Contract Balances and Revenue Recognition Timing
comparisons.peer_summary: Contract assets and liabilities balances reflect timing differences between performance and payment, with contract liabilities of which approximately 55% as of November 3, 2024 related to contracts subject to termination for convenience provisions. Revenue recognized in fiscal year 2024 from prior contract liabilities was $2,440 million, while $2,915 million recognized in fiscal year 2023 came from prior year contract liabilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO disclose significant contract liabilities arising from customer prepayments or advanced payments. MU reports $907 million in customer prepayments and other contract liabilities, while AVGO reports revenue recognized in fiscal year 2024 from prior contract liabilities of $2,440 million, reflecting a much larger volume of deferred revenue. AVGO further discloses that approximately 55% of its contract liabilities related to contracts subject to termination for convenience provisions, a detail not present in MU's disclosure. Both companies attribute changes in these balances to timing differences between performance and payment.
